title: Power Rankings: Big movers include Cavs, Grizz, Sonics
heading: 2005-06 Power Rankings: Week 3

rankings.summaryHtml: Every team has two or three games per season like Saturday's in Dallas. You can stomach it a little easier when you show up for that nightmare undefeated.

rankings.summaryHtml: Finley is back, Ginobili is healing and Spurs' Saturday hex is over. But there's no change at the top because Pistons get same one-loss grace period Spurs got.

rankings.summaryHtml: After spanking Spurs and Pistons, Mavs are up here on merit. Not because a procession of locals, including Sam The Locker-Room Attendant, hunted me down Saturday night to lobby for a top-three slot.

rankings.summaryHtml: There's no shortage of skeptics saying this can't last, and maybe they're right. Or maybe this is the playoff year Mr. Brand, one of the good guys, has long deserved.

rankings.summaryHtml: Cavs haven't lost a home game. They've won three in a row on the road. In other words, an LBJ squad is finally living up to the hype.

rankings.summaryHtml: Grizz need only one more win this month to set a franchise record for November victories. So, yes, addition by subtraction is working so far.

rankings.summaryHtml: I know I said even the best teams have a few nightmares every season, but you still struggle to fathom how a team this talented could lose by 32 at Charlotte. Only the struggles of other top-10 regulars prevented steeper punishment.

rankings.summaryHtml: You know by now that we dispute the existence of a Power Rankings jinx. Wiz fans, though, will be pardoned for their jinx e-mails after being forced to toast their historic rise to No. 3 with three straight road defeats.

rankings.summaryHtml: With two lopsided losses sandwiched around a nice win at GS, Bucks need to beat a beat-up Utah in the trip's finale to add credence to their promising start.

rankings.summaryHtml: With Iverson in MVP form and Webber looking worlds more comfortable beside him -- and a second AI playing sticky D -- that 0-3 start seems like forever ago.

rankings.summaryHtml: Stat we didn't see coming: Nuggets are 4-0 this season when K-Mart sits, after going 10-2 without him last season. With K-Mart? Just 41-36 overall.

rankings.summaryHtml: Baron alluded to it in our discussion in the weekend Dime: Warriors have a rough November with 17 games. The good news? Of the six left, five are at home.

rankings.summaryHtml: Heat's 5-3 record sans Shaq ain't bad. Heat's crunch-time collapse Sunday in Toronto was criminal, Shaq or no Shaq.
rankings.summaryText: Heat's 5-3 record sans Shaq ain't bad. Heat's crunch-time collapse Sunday in Toronto was criminal, Shaq or no Shaq.

rankings.summaryHtml: When will the darkness lift? The brightest spot in a bleak start -- Barbosa -- is suddenly out 2-3 weeks with a knee sprain suffered in a narrow loss to Spurs.

rankings.summaryHtml: Vince has been held under 20 in four straight games. J-Kidd has topped six assists only four times. Not stuff you want to hear entering a five-game trip out West.

rankings.summaryHtml: It's been a decent start, but it's also pretty clear already that (A) McHale has lots to do to win back KG's support and (B) KG trade speculation is going to be a constant.

rankings.summaryHtml: Well, well, well. Sonics suddenly have won four out of five and have a chance to really hush the doomsday talk with nine of the next 11 games at home.

rankings.summaryHtml: If Celts can regularly reproduce the ball they've played against Detroit, maybe these guys (and kids) will be able to hang around for a while in the Titanic, er, Atlantic.

rankings.summaryHtml: Tough as it is to imagine Hornets finding a way back to New Orleans, they've made it back to pesky faster than anyone expected, thanks to Paul's smooth transition.

rankings.summaryHtml: Happy Thanksgiving, indeed. Bulls finally won one on their annual ''circus'' road trip -- to improve to 2-41 on these jaunts since 1999 -- and get a holiday break back home before finishing the six-game swing in Texas over the weekend.

rankings.summaryHtml: Just a hunch, but offense still might be the key for new-look Kings. They averaged only 86.0 ppg in their first five losses, and 110.3 ppg in four wins, before falling Sunday in a 106-104 heartbreaker at Seattle.

rankings.summaryHtml: Rockets know they can recover because they overturned a 6-11 start last season. Of course, T-Mac wasn't ailing then like he is now.

rankings.summaryHtml: Reality is starting to set in for Kobe and Phil. Kwame's out at least two weeks, and Smush is averaging just 8.0 ppg over the past six on 31.5 percent shooting.
